title: Communication and people central to the method in practice
blurb: Apply the communication approach to a scenario (audience, channel, frequency, message, feedback) and spot how each principle works through people.
question: Residents on a half marathon route will lose car access for five hours. The project manager plans to tell them through the event's social media pages. Is this an appropriate application of the communication approach, and why?

teach.body: Good communication avoids misconceptions and needless barriers to change. PRINCE2 7 expects a controlled, two-way flow of information: the project sends the right message to each group, through a channel and at a frequency that suit them, and it gathers feedback from across the project ecosystem. One newsletter to everyone, with no route back, is not communication management.

teach.caption: A communications schedule sets purpose, frequency, channel or format and messaging for each stakeholder group.

teach.body: Formally: part of the PID, it defines the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, the whole project ecosystem, giving a controlled, bidirectional flow of information that engages stakeholders. In plain English: who needs to hear what, why, how and how often, and how we hear back. It is agreed in initiation ('agree the management approaches'), reviewed at each stage boundary and checked at closure for who must be told.

teach.h: Fit the setting and follow the resistance
teach.body: How a team communicates depends on whether it is co-located, remote or hybrid: a distributed team needs meeting times, channels and shared records that work for every location. Pockets of resistance show where communication should be focused; find out why people resist rather than sidelining them. As stages change, influencers and key relationships change too, so the approach is revisited.

Every principle works through people. Learn from experience: much knowledge is hidden in the ecosystem and is best learned socially. Manage by exception: decide at the most local level where the knowledge sits, escalate when other areas are affected, and delegate more as trust grows. Manage by stages: stage ends are good points to review relationships. Focus on products: co-create products to improve adoption. Roles: keep addressing people factors throughout.

teach.h: Each principle through a people lens
head: Principle
People application
Sounds like
teach.caption: Learn this table: people-central questions usually name an action and ask which principle it applies.

items: The route passes two churches, crosses the hospital access road and closes residents' streets for five hours; traders are split between losing and gaining trade.
Kezia Oduya (PM) builds a stakeholder analysis and a schedule giving each group its own purpose, channel, timing and message, with a named route for feedback.
The churches' joint letter is a pocket of resistance, so she meets the clergy to learn why, and the closure timing near the churches becomes part of the planning.
At the end of each stage she reviews the approach, as new groups such as volunteers and runners become the main audience.

teach.text: In people-central questions, match the action to the RIGHT principle: social learning is learn from experience; deciding at the most local level is manage by exception; reviewing relationships at stage ends is manage by stages; co-creating products is focus on products. Options often swap these with a true but mismatched reason.

items: The communication management approach sets means and frequency of communication and feedback across the ecosystem.
Fit purpose, channel, frequency and message to each stakeholder group, and keep the flow two-way.
Communication for distributed teams must work across every location; focus communication where resistance sits.
Agreed in initiation, reviewed at stage boundaries and at closure.
People central: social learning, local decisions, stage-end relationship reviews, co-created products, people factors throughout.

summary: You can now apply the communication approach to a scenario by checking audience, purpose, channel, frequency, message and feedback, and by focusing on resistance. You can also say which principle a people-centred action applies.

A.q: On Carrowford's half marathon, residents on the route, many of them elderly, will be unable to drive out of their streets for five hours on race day. The project manager plans to tell them about the closures through the event's social media pages. Is this an appropriate application of the communication approach, and why?
options: Yes, because social media reaches the largest number of people quickly
Yes, because one channel keeps all the event's messages consistent
No, because each group needs a channel and message that suit it
No, because residents should have been consulted before the route was set
A.why: The communication management approach sets out, for each stakeholder group, the purpose, frequency, channels or format and messaging (3.4). Elderly residents need a channel that reaches them, such as a letter to each home.

whyNot.0: Reach in general is not the test; this particular group may not use social media.
whyNot.1: Consistency matters, but it does not justify a channel that may not reach the people affected.
whyNot.3: The route and date are fixed; the question is how to communicate the closures well.

A.q: On Brennan Mutual's data centre exit, the board's audit committee wants a written update every month. During initiation the project manager adds a monthly written update for the audit committee, with its purpose and format, to the communication management approach. Is this appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because highlight reports have to be sent to the audit committee
Yes, because the schedule sets purpose, frequency and format for each group
No, because the audit committee should receive end stage reports instead
No, because internal audit must stay apart from the project to be independent
A.why: The communication management approach includes a communications schedule and procedures for each stakeholder group: purpose, frequency, channels or format and messaging (3.4).

whyNot.0: Highlight reports go from the project manager to the project board; the audit committee's update is set in the communication approach.
whyNot.2: End stage reports support the board's stage decisions; they do not meet the committee's request for a monthly update.
whyNot.3: Independence does not mean receiving no information; the committee needs regular updates to do its job.

A.q: At Wenmoor Community Health the triage hub nurses decide how to prioritize routine referrals within agreed criteria, and escalate a case to the hub lead when it could affect another locality's capacity. Which principle is being applied through the people element, and why?
options: Learn from experience, because knowledge hidden in the team is learned socially
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships, because people factors are addressed
Manage by stages, because stages mark changes in influencers and key relationships
Manage by exception, because decisions are made at the most local level with the knowledge
A.why: Through the people element, manage by exception means decisions are made at the most local level where the knowledge to make and own them resides, and escalated when they could affect other areas (3.5.1).

whyNot.0: Social learning is how learn from experience works through people, but nothing here is about learning.
whyNot.1: People factors matter throughout, but the action described is about where decisions are made.
whyNot.2: Stage ends are good points to review relationships, but this is a day-to-day decision rule.

B.q: On Carrowford's half marathon, the chair of the city centre traders' association says many shops lose trade when roads close. The project manager asks him why, then works with the association on targeted messages: closure times for each street and an 'open for business' map for race weekend. How well does this apply the communication guidance, and why?
options: It applies it well, because pockets of resistance show where communication should focus
It applies it well, because traders should be represented on the project board
It applies it poorly, because the restaurants that gain trade balance out the shops that lose
It applies it poorly, because messages to traders should come from the title sponsor
B.why: Pockets of resistance are a useful indicator of where communication should be focused, and understanding the reasons shapes the message (3.4).

whyNot.1: Engagement does not require a board seat; the board holds business, user and supplier roles.
whyNot.2: Gains elsewhere do not remove the traders' concern, which is exactly where communication should focus.
whyNot.3: The sponsor's role is branding and funding; communication with stakeholders is planned by the project.

B.q: At the end of the foundations stage on Brennan Mutual's data centre exit, the project manager reviews how the cloud partner's engineers, the operations staff and the member services teams are working together, because member services become the main users affected in the next stage. Which principle is being applied through the people element, and why?
options: Learn from experience, because lessons should be recorded at the end of each stage
Manage by stages, because stage ends are good points to review key relationships
Manage by exception, because delegation grows as trust in key relationships grows
Focus on products, because co-created products are adopted more readily
B.why: Through the people element, stages often mark a change in influencers and key relationships, so stage ends are good points to review how people interact with each other and the wider organization (3.5.1).

whyNot.0: Lessons may be reviewed at the stage end, but the action is reviewing relationships because the influencers are changing.
whyNot.2: Delegation adapting to trust is the exception principle; no delegation is being changed here.
whyNot.3: No product is being co-created; the review is of working relationships.

B.q: At Tarnside College much of what the estates team knows about how the campus really works is not written down anywhere. The project manager starts a fortnightly informal session where the contractor's site team, the estates team and the curriculum team share what they have found out about the building and its users. Which principle is being applied through the people element, and why?
options: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships, because it brings three teams together
Manage by exception, because each team decides locally within its tolerances
Learn from experience, because hidden knowledge in the ecosystem is learned socially
Focus on products, because users are involved in designing the building's products
B.why: Through the people element, learn from experience recognizes that valuable knowledge is hidden in the project ecosystem and is best learned socially, in a collaborative, knowledge-sharing environment (3.5.1).

whyNot.0: Relationships may benefit, but the purpose stated is sharing knowledge that is not written down.
whyNot.1: Local decision-making is not involved; the sessions share knowledge.
whyNot.3: Co-design of products is not described; the sessions share what people know about the building.

C.q: On Calderbrook's permit project, the communication plan is a monthly newsletter sent to all staff and councillors, with no way for readers to respond. Ward councillors worried that older residents will be left behind have no route to raise their concerns with the project. Is this an appropriate application of the communication approach, and why?
options: Yes, because a single newsletter gives every reader the same message
Yes, because councillors can raise their concerns through the project board
No, because the newsletter should go out weekly during the private beta
No, because the approach should give a two-way flow, including feedback
C.why: The communication management approach defines the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, the project ecosystem: a controlled, bidirectional flow (3.4).

whyNot.0: Consistency does not fix the lack of any route for feedback from an important group.
whyNot.1: Ward councillors are not on the board, so that is not a route open to them.
whyNot.2: Frequency is not the problem; a weekly one-way newsletter would still give no route back.

C.q: On Brennan Mutual's data centre exit, the team is split between Edinburgh and Pune. The project manager decides that all team communication will happen at the Edinburgh office's daily 5pm meeting, which is late at night in Pune, with no notes shared afterwards. Is this appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because one daily meeting keeps everyone on the same information
Yes, because the Pune delivery lead can pass the main points on to his team
No, because team communication should suit co-located, remote or hybrid set-ups
No, because daily meetings belong to the supplier's methods, not to PRINCE2
C.why: How teams communicate depends on whether they are co-located, remote or hybrid (3.4). A meeting at night in Pune, with no shared record, excludes most of the delivery team.

whyNot.0: One meeting only helps if people can attend it; most of the Pune team will not.
whyNot.1: Passing points on second-hand loses the two-way flow and the detail the engineers need.
whyNot.3: The method does not forbid daily meetings; the problem is that this arrangement does not work for one location.

C.q: At Fernhollow Foods two recipes will be made by a co-manufacturer. The project manager has the co-manufacturer, Fernhollow's operations team and the chefs agree the product descriptions for those recipes together, including what the factory needs at handover. Is this an appropriate application of the 'focus on products' principle through the people element, and why?
options: Yes, because co-creating products improves adoption and reduces handover risk
Yes, because the senior supplier approves all of the project's product descriptions
No, because the product descriptions should be written by the PM in initiation
No, because the co-manufacturer's own specification should be used unchanged
C.why: Co-creating products, with agreed product descriptions, with the business, user and supplier communities unites their perspectives, improves development and adoption and reduces handover risk (3.5.1).

whyNot.1: Approval responsibilities are set product by product; the senior supplier does not approve every description.
whyNot.2: Product descriptions are written as products are planned, with input from those who know them, not by the PM alone.
whyNot.3: The co-manufacturer's specification is an input, but Fernhollow's needs must also be reflected.

reteach.title: Who, why, how, when, what, and back again
reteach.question: For any group in the scenario, can you say who they are, why you are talking to them, how, how often, what you will say, and how they will reply?

blocks.h: Five questions and a return path
blocks.body: WHO comes from the stakeholder analysis. WHY is the purpose. HOW is the channel or format that suits that group. WHEN is the frequency. WHAT is the message. Then the return path: a way for that group to give feedback, which the project acts on. If any of these is missing or one-size-fits-all, the communication approach is applied poorly.

blocks.text: An option that praises a channel because it is quick, cheap or consistent is a lure if that channel does not reach the group in the stem.

explain.body: The communications schedule and procedures set, for each stakeholder group, the purpose, frequency, channel or format and messaging. Critical groups get a procedure that fits how they must work.

test.q: On Carrowford's half marathon, the police events planning officer must be able to agree road-closure decisions quickly. The project manager sets up a weekly planning call during the build-up stage and a direct line to the race control room on race day, and records both in the communication management approach. Which statement explains why this is appropriate?
options: Pockets of resistance show where the project's communication should focus
Each stakeholder group needs its own purpose, frequency and channel
Highlight reports keep the project board informed of the stage's progress
The business, user and supplier interests are represented on the board
test.why: The communications schedule and procedures set purpose, frequency, channels or format and messaging for each stakeholder group (3.4). The police need a fast, reliable route.

whyNot.0: The police are not resisting; the action fits communication to a critical group's needs.
whyNot.2: Highlight reports go to the board; this procedure is for an external stakeholder.
whyNot.3: The police are not board members; this is about communicating with a stakeholder.

explain.body: The communication approach is agreed in initiation, reviewed at each stage boundary as stakeholders and relationships change, and checked at closure for who needs to be told.

test.q: At Tarnside College, the fit-out stage brings instructors, apprentice employers and the equipment supplier into close contact with the project for the first time. At the end of the structural works stage the project manager reviews and updates the communication management approach. Which statement explains why this is appropriate?
options: The approach is reviewed at stage boundaries as stakeholders and relationships change
The approach is created when the project closes, so that everyone affected is told
The approach is owned by the senior supplier, who manages the equipment supplier
The approach is used by team managers to report their progress to the PM
test.why: The communication management approach is agreed in initiation and reviewed at stage boundaries, when influencers and key relationships often change (3.4, 3.5.1).

whyNot.1: It is created in initiation; at closure it is checked for who needs to be notified.
whyNot.2: The project manager prepares the approach as part of the PID; the senior supplier does not own it.
whyNot.3: Team managers report through checkpoint reports, not through the communication approach.

explain.body: Co-located teams pick up information naturally. Remote and hybrid teams need meeting times, channels and shared records that work for every location and work pattern.

test.q: At Wenmoor Community Health most team members work rotas across three localities and can usually only join online at lunchtime. The project manager keeps team meetings to a short online lunchtime slot and posts every decision to a shared online space that staff can read between visits. Which statement explains why this is appropriate?
options: Structured team-building exercises can speed up the forming of a new team
Decisions should be taken at the most local level that has the knowledge
Pockets of resistance indicate where communication should be focused
How a team communicates should suit its co-located, remote or hybrid set-up
test.why: How teams communicate depends on whether they are co-located, remote or hybrid (3.4). These arrangements fit a dispersed team on rotas.

whyNot.0: No team-building exercise is described; the action shapes routine communication.
whyNot.1: Local decision-making is manage by exception; the stem is about how information reaches people.
whyNot.2: Nobody is resisting here; the action fits communication to the way people work.

explain.body: Through the people element, manage by exception means the extent of delegation depends on confidence and trust in key relationships, and it changes over the project as people's skills grow.

test.q: On Calderbrook's permit project the project manager is new to projects of this size. As she delivers the first three stages well, the project board gives her wider authority, with larger stage tolerances, for the final stage. Which principle is being applied through the people element, and why?
options: Manage by stages, because the board authorizes each stage at its boundary
Learn from experience, because the board has learned from the earlier stages
Manage by exception, because delegation adapts to trust and growing skills
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships, because her role has changed
test.why: Through the people element, the extent of delegation depends on the confidence and trust in key relationships and adapts over the project as skills grow (3.5.1). Tolerances are the means of delegation.

whyNot.0: Stage authorization is manage by stages, but the stem is about how much authority is delegated.
whyNot.1: Experience is involved, but the action is changing delegated limits because of trust, which is exception.
whyNot.3: Her role is the same; what changes is the size of her delegated authority.
